comment: Centralisation is an implementation topology and should not form part of the definition of a registry. The current definition is also inconsistent with the Guidance itself: p. 54 states that registries are authoritative and canonical constructs while “whether they are realised centrally, in a federated manner, or as a hybrid remains a national implementation choice.” The glossary should reflect the same topology-neutral principle.

public.text: Centralisation is an implementation topology and should not form part of the definition of a registry. The current definition is also inconsistent with the Guidance itself: p. 54 states that registries are authoritative and canonical constructs while “whether they are realised centrally, in a federated manner, or as a hybrid remains a national implementation choice.” The glossary should reflect the same topology-neutral principle.
public.suggestedRevision: Replace with: “Registry: A governed and authoritative information capability that captures, stores and maintains, or provides authoritative access to, the identifiers and core attributes of health facilities, health service users, health products and/or the health workforce using a predefined canonical minimum dataset. A registry may be implemented centrally, in a federated manner or through a hybrid architecture, provided that authoritative sources, stewardship, identity resolution and conformance requirements are clearly defined.”
